thread.title: Apple: Are People Sick of Expensive Phones?

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Are People Sick of Expensive Phones?
text:
Photo: Photographer: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg Are consumers tiring of rising smartphone prices? Could be, Nomura Instinet analysts argued in a Monday note that examined questions about demand for the high-end iPhone X. 
“We see several indications the market elasticity is falling,” they wrote. “ Apple’s (AAPL) iPhone [average selling prices] have climbed from $645 in FY16; we model $742 in FY18. We do not believe it is coincidence that the highest end of the product portfolio, the X, is the model that is flagging.”
• The analysts noted questions about demand for Samsung ’s new flagship S9, which is less expensive than the X, based on reports of preorder levels lower than those of previous models. Reviewers have characterized that phone as a solid high-end Android offering , but not a big technological step forward. 
And “domestic Chinese smartphone vendors appear to be gearing production toward the middle tier of the smartphone market,” the analysts wrote. 
• Given the iPhone’s popularity, it’s likely that increasing prices will be crucial for the Barron’s Next 50 company. Offering customers a range of phones at a range of prices , and then making upgrading as attractive as possible, would be key. 
• The big picture for Apple phone demand, however, remains positive, according to the analysts: “The iOS user base has grown at a similar or better pace in the iPhone 8/X cycle than in the 7 cycle,” they wrote. “This should sustain Apple’s Services growth, and ultimately restore iPhone volume growth. Replacement rates will not lengthen forever.”
